rationale: `SELECT Id, Status FROM Orders WHERE Id = @id` through FromSqlRaw: a readable statement with a resolvable target table (Orders). Must resolve to a data-access operation.
`INSERT INTO Orders (...)` through ExecuteSqlRaw, with a resolvable target table and column list. Must resolve to a data-access operation.
`UPDATE Orders SET Status = @status WHERE Id = @id` through ExecuteSqlRaw, with a resolvable target table. Must resolve to a data-access operation.
`EXEC usp_RebuildOrderTotals` through ExecuteSqlRaw: a stored-procedure call naming a resolvable operation target. Must resolve to a data-access operation.
`DELETE FROM [Orders] WHERE Status = 'Archived'`; the bracketed identifier unquotes to the same Orders target SelectOrder reads. Must resolve to a data-access operation.

FromSqlInterpolated with a run-time table name; syntactically a SQL data-access call exactly like the five resolvable statements above, but no node may be minted for a target only known at run time. Must publish as unresolved, never as a confirmed operation naming a fabricated target.

A plain property returning the connection-string constant; not a data-access operation at all, even though it sits beside real SQL statements in the same class. An unambiguous negative for the persistence classifier.
